_comment: One scope statement per expert, written from the role boundaries in PLAN-role-experts.md and not from any checklist. The judge uses it to tell a finding in the domain from a finding in another domain; the plain-lens arm is told it.

architect.name: system architecture
architect.scope: The whole system: components and services, the flows between them, platform and framework choices, AWS service fit and the Well-Architected concerns (reliability, failure isolation and retries, idempotency, state placement, data-layer tenancy, performance, cost, operations). Not code-level structure, not single bugs, not security vulnerabilities, not test quality.

softarch.name: software architecture
softarch.scope: Code components: module boundaries, who may import whom, dependency direction, layering, public contracts between modules or services and their compatibility, data ownership between modules. Not runtime topology, not single-function craft, not security vulnerabilities, not test quality.

developer.name: engineering craft
developer.scope: Craft of new or substantially rewritten production code: SOLID, clean code, simplicity, duplication, naming, error and fallback handling, new dependencies, speculative generality. Style that a linter or formatter would catch is NOT in scope. Not module-level architecture, not system topology, not security vulnerabilities, not test quality.

quality.name: test and evaluation quality
quality.scope: Whether tests, evals and CI gates can be trusted: assertions that cannot fail, flaky patterns, weakened gates, contract tests, and how LLM-agent outputs are evaluated (repeats, judge calibration, trajectory). Not production-code design, not security vulnerabilities, not system topology.
